objectives: Identify shared rimes in taught br-words and familiar partner words.
Sort words by vowel-and-ending patterns rather than by onset alone.
Decode every word fully after sorting.
Use controlled word groups to read a short, accurate line.
concepts: A rime includes the vowel and any sounds after it.
Words can share an onset but have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Sorting supports reading only when each full word is decoded.

definitions.definition: The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
A group of words sharing a rime, such as brick and trick (-ick).
The consonant or consonant blend before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share the -ick rime but have different onsets.
They share the -ag rime; their onsets differ.
They share -im, but the first consonants differ.

commonMistakes: Grouping all br-words together despite different rimes.
Looking only at the first two letters.
Ignoring the ending consonant when sorting.
Reading by rhyme without decoding the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to find a rime.
Same onset does not mean same word family.
Different onsets can share a rime.
revisionPoints: Sort by the rime, then read each whole word.

steps: Listen to or read each target word carefully.
Say or map each sound in the correct order.
Complete the task and explain the sound or text evidence.
Reread or repeat the word to check accuracy.
